blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Constitutional bodies derive their powers and authority directly from the Constitution of India.
The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is responsible for conducting examinations for appointments to All-India and Central Services.
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) audits all receipts and expenditures of the Government of India and the state governments.
The Finance Commission recommends the distribution of financial resources and tax proceeds between the Union and the States.
The Attorney General of India serves as the chief legal advisor to the Union Government, while the Advocate General functions similarly for State Governments.

blocks.content: Constitutional Bodies are those bodies which are directly mentioned in the Constitution of India and derive their authority, powers and existence from the Constitution itself.
These bodies are created to ensure:

items:
• Smooth functioning of democracy
  • Accountability of the government
  • Transparency in administration
  • Balance of power between organs of government
Balance of power between organs of government

blocks.content: They play a vital role in maintaining constitutional governance and preventing misuse of power.
A Constitutional Body is an institution:

items:
• Established by the Constitution
  • Whose powers are mentioned in the Constitution
  • Which cannot be abolished by ordinary law
  • Whose independence is protected by constitutional provisions
Whose powers are mentioned in the Constitution
Which cannot be abolished by ordinary law
Whose independence is protected by constitutional provisions

blocks.content: Any change related to these bodies requires a Constitutional Amendment.
Major Constitutional Bodies in India are:
The Union Public Service Commission is a central constitutional body responsible for recruiting civil servants for the Union Government.
They are appointed by the President of India.
There is no fixed number of members mentioned in the Constitution.

items:

  • Audits State Government accounts
  • Audits public sector undertakings

Submits reports to President and Governors

• Ensures financial accountability
  • Prevents misuse of public funds
  • Strengthens parliamentary control

blocks.content: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280. It is appointed by the President every 5 years.

items:
• Distribution of taxes between Centre and States
  • Grants-in-aid to States
  • Recommend fiscal reforms
  • Strengthen federal financial relations
Distribution of taxes between Centre and States

blocks.content: The Attorney General is the highest law officer of India. Article 76 deals with the Attorney General.
He is appointed by the President.

items:
• Legal advisor to Government of India
  • Represents Government in Supreme Court
  • Gives legal opinions
  • Performs duties assigned by President
Legal advisor to Government of India

blocks.content: The Advocate General is the highest law officer of a State. Article 165 deals with Advocate General.
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ATTORNEY GENERAL AND ADVOCATE GENERAL

items: Constitutional Articles: UPSC (Articles 315–323), CAG (Article 148), Finance Commission (Article 280), Attorney General (Article 76), and Advocate General (Article 165).
Tenure & Independence: CAG and UPSC members enjoy security of tenure to ensure unbiased function without executive interference.
Right of Audience: The Attorney General has the right to speak in both Houses of Parliament but does not possess voting rights.

• Ensure transparency
  • Maintain checks and balances
  • Prevent misuse of power
  • Strengthen democracy
  • Promote good governance

• Political interference
  • Delay in appointments
  • Lack of autonomy
  • Inadequate resources

• Transparent appointment process
  • Fixed tenure security
  • Greater autonomy
  • Reduced executive control

blocks.content: Constitutional Bodies are the backbone of Indian democracy. They ensure accountability, transparency and rule of law.
Strengthening these institutions is essential for strong democratic governance.
